# v1.21.4b1 — Optional AC PV meter energy counter

Development beta for [issue #16](https://github.com/PlainSeer/ha-alphaess-modbus-tcp/issues/16), following the related [upstream report](https://github.com/senalse/ha-alphaess-modbus/issues/25). Hardware validation of the counter's physical direction is still needed.

## What changes

- Add **PV Meter Energy (0x0092)** (`total_energy_pv_meter_0092`), a separate lifetime energy sensor reading `0x0092–0x0093` as unsigned 32-bit at 0.01 kWh per count.
- The new sensor is **disabled and not polled by default**. Existing installations retain their current polling unless it is enabled.
- When enabled, use a separate read at the configured 60-second cadence. An unsupported address or malformed response makes the new counter unknown without invalidating existing counter reads; failed attempts wait a full interval before retrying. A slow or timed-out optional read can still delay a poll cycle while enabled.
- Preserve the existing `0x0090` sensor's identity, mapping and history. No inverter commands, house-load filters, daily-energy calculations or PredBat settings are changed. This beta does not address the remaining positive peaks in issue #10.

## How to compare

1. Install the beta through HACS and restart Home Assistant as usual.
2. Find the disabled **PV Meter Energy (0x0092)** sensor under the AlphaESS device's entities and enable it **while no dispatch is active**. Home Assistant can reload the integration when a disabled entity is enabled.
3. Allow the next scheduled poll, then record both this counter and **Total Energy Feed to Grid (PV)** at the start and end of matching daylight and overnight periods.
4. Compare the increases with integrated **Active Power PV Meter**, and the separate PV inverter's energy reading where available. Report the times, values, inverter model/firmware and any unknown readings in [issue #16](https://github.com/PlainSeer/ha-alphaess-modbus-tcp/issues/16).

AlphaESS documents these as opposite PV-meter energy directions. The reports indicate `0x0092` tracks PV production on some AC-coupled installations, but this is not yet established for every model or meter arrangement. The new sensor is deliberately named by address. Do not add it to existing PV energy totals or use it as an Energy dashboard source until its meaning is confirmed on the installation.

Regression tests cover word order/scaling, separate identities, disabled/default polling, existing read sequences and values, rejected/malformed/failed reads, retry spacing and recovery. Simulated checks do not replace hardware validation.
